newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil futures end at day's low.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil futures end at day's low.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed with a soft tone, chipping at the bottom of the day's $2 range at the close but failing to make any significant impact, traders said.
The December gas oil contract last traded 75 cents down at the days low of $216.25 a tonne.

Some brokers saw potential for gas oil to shed a couple of dollars but said the downside was limited with generally positive fundamentals -- including cold weather and largely bullish stock figures -- bolstering prices.
Brent crude offered little direction hovering in mid-range for much of the day with the prospect of Iraq's re-entry into the market looking more likely to be absorbed.
However, there was still some uncertainty blocking any concerted move either up or down.
"No one wants to be caught pushing things too much," one broker said.
Jan Brent was trading six cents up at $22.80 a barrel at 1758 GMT.

Iraq announced at the biannual OPEC meeting in Vienna, which kicked off on Wednesday, that it could resume oil exports "within a matter of weeks" and that it expected to export between 700,000 and 800,000 barrels per day.
OPEC sources have said they expect current production quotas to be rolled over into 1997, although there was disagreement whether this would be for six months or one year.
